question: Should OpenClaw accept the legacy Installed Apps opt-in reset and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout after the branch is refreshed?
rationale: The code path is focused and privacy-protective, but disabling existing opt-ins and adding a Play Data Safety release lane are upgrade and release-policy choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Resolve conflicts and confirm rollout
options.body: Rebase the PR, preserve current Android settings/release behavior, then merge after maintainer approval of the reset, disclosure copy, Data Safety CSV, and privacy-policy alignment.

options.title: Revise disclosure first
options.body: Request wording, placement, consent-version, or release-lane changes if Play review or product policy needs a different prominent-disclosure shape.

options.title: Hold the PR
options.body: Keep the branch paused if the external Play Console or privacy-policy materials are not ready to ship with the code.

recommendation.title: Resolve conflicts and confirm rollout
recommendation.body: Rebase the PR, preserve current Android settings/release behavior, then merge after maintainer approval of the reset, disclosure copy, Data Safety CSV, and privacy-policy alignment.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Android release and settings work makes this the best available routing owner for the conflict and rollout decision.
